question: 35 men can do a piece of work in 8 days. Find the time required by 16 men to do four times the work.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the MDH formula: (M₁ × D₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) ÷ W₂

⇒ (35 × 8) ÷ 1 = (16 × D₂) ÷ 4

⇒ 280 = 4 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 280 ÷ 4 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 Days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial workers (M₁) = 35 men, Time taken (D₁) = 8 days

New workers (M₂) = 16 men, New work (W₂) = 4 × Original work

⇒ Total Original Work = 35 × 8 = 280 units

⇒ New Total Work required = 4 × 280 = 1120 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of 16 men = 16 units per day

⇒ Time required by 16 men = New Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 1120 ÷ 16 = 70 Days

**∴ The correct answer is 70 Days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Formula

(M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is Men, D is Days, H is Hours, and W is the Work done.

Work Efficiency Rule

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. A person taking less time has a higher efficiency: E₁ × T₁ = E₂ × T₂.

Group Work Concept

If multiple people work together uniformly, their combined efficiency is simply the sum of their individual efficiencies: ETₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ.
